name: Finished graphic holds at least 2 s before it leaves
when: Any card, label, lower third or pop graphic that animates in and then out
action: After the entrance settles, keep the graphic fully still and readable for at least 2 s before its exit starts. Entrance 0.3–0.6 s ease-out, exit 0.2–0.4 s ease-in (exit shorter).
why: A graphic that starts leaving as soon as it lands is never read; the hold is what the viewer actually uses.
evidence_note: One tool's motion-graphics skill (FableCut) states these as house defaults; no measured study.
conflict_note: Entrance/exit bands only confirm R-202/G-033. The new part is the ≥2 s settled hold. For reading-heavy cards G-012/G-026 (word-count holds) are stricter and win.

name: Exposure check on every rendered still/scene: median luma 0.35–0.50
when: QC pass on the rendered video (one sampled frame per beat/scene)
action: Measure luma (Rec.709, 0–1) on a mid-scene frame. Flag: median outside 0.35–0.50 (unless the scene is meant to be night/dark), more than ~1% of pixels at pure white (clipped highlights), more than ~2% at pure black (crushed shadows). Flag only — do not auto-correct.
why: Gives KANG a numeric exposure guard for mixed stock/phone/AI stills that today pass unchecked; the numbers are cheap to compute with FFmpeg signalstats.
evidence_note: Thresholds are the reading guide of FableCut's built-in scopes tool, not a broadcast standard. Treat as starting values; dark temple interiors and night shots need an exemption tag.
conflict_note: R-213/R-267 say set exposure with scopes and match to a hero shot but give no numbers; T-002 supplies them.

name: Colour-cast check on neutral scenes (cast strength ≤ 0.03)
when: QC pass on scenes that should look neutral (white walls, overcast sky, marble)
action: Compute the midtone colour cast (mean chroma direction of mid-luma pixels). If its strength is above ~0.03 on a scene tagged neutral, flag it and suggest moving temperature against the cast (orange/yellow → cooler, blue/cyan → warmer) and tint against green/magenta. Leave skin-led and golden-hour scenes warm on purpose.
why: Mixed sources (phone, stock, AI) arrive with different white balance; a cast jump between consecutive stills reads as a continuity error.
evidence_note: FableCut gives the 0.03 cast threshold; samuelgursky's pre-balance tool gives the 'leave midtones warm' caution. Both tool docs, no study.
conflict_note: Keep T-012 (midtones warm) in mind: do not neutralise skin or sunset beats.

name: Caption tail ≈ 0.25 s, never into the next caption; new block at a ≥0.6 s pause
when: Building caption cues from word timings (captions_hindi.srt and pop words)
action: Start a new caption block when: a pause of ≥0.6 s occurs, a sentence ends, or a comma appears after the block already has ≥3 words, or the block would exceed its line/second limit. Let each caption stay ~0.25 s after its last spoken word, but end it before the next cue starts; snap starts and ends to whole frames. Re-make captions after the cut is final (a later cut shortens a cue without re-timing its words).
why: A small tail lets slow readers finish; snapping and no-overlap avoid one-frame flashes; regenerating after the cut keeps words in sync.
evidence_note: FableCut caption generator defaults (documented behaviour). No reading study behind the 0.25 s / 0.6 s numbers.
conflict_note: R-247 breaks a word-level subtitle line at a 0.7 s pause; T-004 uses 0.6 s for phrase captions. Suggest 0.6 s for long-form phrase captions, keep R-247's 0.7 s for word-by-word reels. G-014 (min duration / 2-frame gap) still wins when the tail would create a <2-frame gap.

name: Music duck starts before the voice and bridges short gaps
when: Music bed under narration
action: Begin the duck ~0.3 s before each spoken phrase, hold it through the phrase, release over ~0.6 s after. Treat speech gaps shorter than ~0.5–1 s as still speaking so the music does not pump up between words. Typical depth −10 to −12 dB; detect speech above about −40 dBFS.
why: Ducking that reacts after the first syllable makes the first word fight the music; un-bridged gaps cause audible pumping.
evidence_note: Two tool defaults agree on depth (FableCut −10/−12 dB; VectCut 7.5–10 dB). Pre-roll and gap bridging are tool behaviour, not studies.
licence: MIT (FableCut) / Apache-2.0 (VectCutAPI repo; its skill folder MIT)
conflict_note: R-103 gives 10–50 ms attack; that is the compressor's attack once triggered. T-005 is about *when* the duck starts (look-ahead) — both can hold.

name: Long-form YouTube master: H.264 CRF ~18, keyframe every 0.5 s, AAC 384 kbps 48 kHz
when: Final 16:9 YouTube export from the FFmpeg renderer
action: Encode 1920×1080 H.264 at CRF ~18 (constant quality, not a fixed low bitrate), force a keyframe at least every 0.5 s, audio AAC-LC 384 kbps at 48 kHz. For 9:16 reels: CRF ~19 with a maxrate cap of ~20–25 Mb/s, AAC 256 kbps; warn when a reel exceeds the platform's length.
why: YouTube re-encodes everything; a high-quality, seek-friendly upload with dense keyframes keeps the re-encode clean and makes chapter seeking fast.
evidence_note: Tool export-preset table (FableCut). YouTube's own published upload guidance should be checked before treating as 🟡.
conflict_note: R-272 gives VBR 2-pass bitrate bands (10–24 Mbps 1080p). Either is fine; CRF 18 usually lands inside that band for travel footage. Pick one method per profile, not both.

name: One entrance family per video; ≤2 fonts, ≤3 transition types, 1–2 highlight colours
when: Planning text animations, fonts, transitions and caption accent colours for a whole video
action: Choose one entrance style for titles and one for small pop graphics and keep them for the whole video. Use at most 2 typefaces, at most 3 transition types, and 1–2 accent/highlight colours used consistently (a colour may map to a meaning, e.g. one per time of day).
why: A different animation, font or colour on every element is the clearest 'auto-generated' signal and makes the video feel noisy.
evidence_note: Three tool skills agree (FableCut presets advice, cli-anything-capcut anti-slop list, cutcli TikTok rules). Opinion, not measured.
conflict_note: FableCut's edit-video skill also says 'vary the font per title' to avoid a machine look — that contradicts its own motion-graphics advice and the other two sources. Propose: max 2 fonts (one display, one caption), variety comes from size/weight, not new typefaces.

name: Lower-third build order: plate → text → accent line
when: Place-name or person lower third
action: Animate in layers: the backing bar grows to full width in ~0.5 s ease-out; the text rises in ~0.2 s after the bar starts; a thin accent rule draws on from ~0.3 s to ~1.0 s. Exit everything together with a ~0.4 s fade. Use 2–3 colours: one accent, one neutral, one translucent backing (~60–65% opaque).
why: Layered entrance reads as designed; text appearing before its plate looks broken.
evidence_note: Worked example in FableCut's motion-graphics skill; numbers are that example's, not a standard.
conflict_note: R-385 gives a ~12-frame slide-in for the whole lower third; T-008 adds the inner order and offsets.

name: Motion blur only on fast moves; off on slow Ken Burns drifts
when: Deciding motion blur for moving elements (renderer or AE/Premiere package)
action: Add motion blur (shutter ~180°, ~8 samples; 12–16 only for very fast spins; 360° for a deliberate smear) to whip moves, fly-ins and fast spins. Leave it off on slow drifts and Ken Burns moves where it is invisible but costs render time.
why: On an i5 CPU render, blur on every layer multiplies render time for no visible gain.
evidence_note: FableCut motion-graphics skill.
conflict_note: CONFLICT with R-304 (blur ON on every moving layer). Proposed resolution for KANG: R-304 for fast moves, T-009 exemption for slow drifts (<~2% frame width per frame), because of CPU budget.

name: Transition ≤ 1/3 of the shorter neighbouring clip, hard cap 2 s
when: Any dissolve, wipe or other transition between two clips/stills
action: Default length ~0.5 s. Never longer than one third of the shorter of the two clips it joins, and never over 2 s. The clips must abut (no gap) and have enough handle media under the transition (see T-011).
why: A long transition on a short clip means the viewer never sees the clip clean; gaps break transitions in NLE import.
evidence_note: cutcli cookbook (1/3 rule), editly default 0.5 s, and the Premiere guidance that premiere-pro-mcp quotes from adb-mcp (≤2 s, no gaps). Tool conventions.
conflict_note: R-354 allows transitions 0.5–1.5 s; T-010 adds the per-clip ratio cap, which binds first on short beats.

name: Leave handles: ≥8 frames picture, ≥48 frames audio beyond every used range
when: Writing source in/out points into the Premiere xmeml package
action: When a clip is trimmed from longer media, check there are at least 8 frames of unused picture and 48 frames of unused audio past each in/out point. Report (do not block) any join that lacks them, because a dissolve, slip, audio crossfade or room-tone fill there will fail or need a freeze.
why: Audio needs far more handle than picture because crossfades and ambience reach past the picture cut; the editor finds missing handles too late otherwise.
frequency: Every trimmed clip in the package
evidence_note: Handle floors from a Resolve turnover/handle-report tool; industry convention, not a study.

name: Neutral balance first; midtones stay warm; flag clipping, never auto-fix
when: Automatic colour pre-balance of mixed stills/clips
action: Balance black point first, then white point, per channel, from a mid-scene frame; group shots by setup/source and pick a hero per group. Do not neutralise midtones (skin should stay on the warm skin line). Automatic steps may only do this neutral balance — no curves, vignettes, saturation pushes or secondaries. Clipped highlights or crushed shadows are flagged for the human, not 'fixed'.
why: Neutralising midtones turns faces grey; an automatic step that also stylises cannot know a dark shot was dark on purpose.
evidence_note: Assistant-colourist practice as encoded in a Resolve MCP tool; not measured.
conflict_note: Fits ORDER.md (engine flags, human decides).

name: At most ~2.5 competing sound streams
when: Mixing voice, music, ambience and SFX at any moment
action: Count as competing any stream within 12 dB of the loudest one at that moment; streams further down are a bed/texture. Flag moments with more than 2–3 competing streams (e.g. voice + loud SFX + music not ducked).
why: Listeners follow about two and a half sound streams; beyond that everything becomes mush and the narration is lost.
evidence_note: Murch's long-standing 'two-and-a-half' observation as implemented by a Resolve audit; the tool itself says it is an observation, not a measured constant.
conflict_note: Complements R-212/R-222 (SFX budget) and R-449 (scenic audio policy).

name: Flag a timeline with zero split edits
when: QC of the assembled package (narration + visuals) at scene changes
action: Classify each scene join as J-cut (next sound early), L-cut (previous sound lingers), straight, or unpaired (picture cut with continuous sound). If every join is straight, flag it. No target ratio — just require that place changes use at least some split edits (ambience lead-ins).
why: An all-straight timeline is usually one nobody has listened to; sound leading picture makes place changes feel natural.
evidence_note: Resolve MCP split-edit audit; craft convention.
conflict_note: R-262 sets the 6–12 frame offset; T-014 is only the 'not zero' audit.

name: Critic reports what it cannot see; no single composite score
when: Designing the rules-engine critic output (step_4 engine report)
action: Always list emotion and story as NOT_ASSESSED (Murch's Rule of Six weights them ~51% and ~23%), list unimplemented checks as NOT_IMPLEMENTED (never as passes), and state coverage ('n of 6 criteria, covering x% of the decision'). Order findings by scope (whole video → scene → moment) and weight, not by count. Avoid publishing one averaged percentage as if it described the cut.
why: A single score built only from the measurable ~26% looks like a quality verdict it cannot give.
evidence_note: Design stance of the Resolve MCP 'rule_of_six_audit'; weights are Murch's (already in package science files).
conflict_note: PLAN-RELEVANT: step_4 engine currently prints one % score (e.g. Dwarika 36.4%). Proposal: keep per-layer pass/fail + coverage line, drop or demote the single %.

name: Cutaways sit inside one beat, never straddle two
when: Placing B-roll/stock/stills against narration beats (visuals_beats CSV)
action: Every inserted visual starts and ends inside a single narration beat; a beat marked protected (e.g. on-camera moment, deity frame) is never covered; if a visual has an explicit beat index, place it there or not at all — never silently move it to another beat.
why: A cutaway that crosses a beat boundary illustrates two ideas at once and breaks S-007 timing.
evidence_note: Placement contract of the Resolve MCP B-roll planner.

name: Music-cut montage: cut on phrases by default, every 2 beats when retiming
when: Montage sections without narration (intro/outro, travel montage, reels)
action: Default cut points = musical phrase boundaries; for a faster section use bars, every beat only for a deliberate 'relentless' moment. When retiming shots to the beat: 2 beats per shot as default, 1 for fast reels, 4 for calm sections. Shots under ~0.6 s read as flashes. If all cuts feel one beat early, check the downbeat offset (pickup bar).
why: Cuts that resolve with the music feel inevitable rather than merely synced.
evidence_note: Two tool docs (Resolve MCP beat-cut planner; FableCut beats/retime).
conflict_note: Long-form narrated sections follow Q-001/Q-003 instead.

name: Don't place cuts on raw Whisper word times
when: Cutting or syncing narration/captions from ASR word timestamps
action: Use ASR word times to know *which* words exist, but not *where* to cut: they can be off by about ±0.3 s and pad word ends. Refine edges to the waveform/speech onset before cutting. Treat a silence ≥0.25 s inside a sentence as a possible restart. Gaps <0.6 s between blocks of one thought may be joined into one clip.
why: Cutting on padded ASR times leaves breaths and clipped syllables.
evidence_note: Idea and numbers from AdamGarceau/resolve-toolkit (no LICENSE file); written fully in own words, no text/code copied.
conflict_note: AdamGarceau also uses zero in-pad for tight talking-head cuts; that conflicts with R-346 (0.25 s pre-pad) and is NOT proposed for KANG narration.

name: Presenter/talking clips: min 1.5 s per framing, re-frame by 10 s
when: Clips of a person talking (presenter, local guide) where KANG adds punch-in/out framing
action: 16:9: no framing change faster than 1.5 s (anti-flicker); force a new framing or cutaway by ~10 s. 9:16: min 1.0 s, max ~5 s. For calm personal stories hold each framing ≥4 s. A new shot needs ~3–5 s to be taken in.
why: Switching too fast feels dizzy; holding a static framing too long loses attention.
evidence_note: Numbers from a podcast punch-in skill (AdamGarceau/resolve-toolkit, no licence). Own words only.
conflict_note: Q-001 (no shot over ~7 s in narrated pieces) is stricter for narration-over-visuals; T-019 is only for on-camera talking clips.

name: Noise/voice isolation at 30–50%, not full strength
when: Cleaning location audio or noisy narration
action: Apply AI voice isolation / noise reduction at roughly 30–50% wet; full strength creates watery artefacts. Then level and limit (VO peak target per R-451).
why: Partial isolation removes room noise while keeping a natural voice.
evidence_note: Resolve Fairlight chain notes in AdamGarceau/resolve-toolkit; own words.
conflict_note: R-438 uses 80% dry/wet for manual NR — different tool, different scale; keep both as starting points per tool.

name: Humanise TTS narration: room tone ≈ −45 dB, varied pauses 300–600 ms
when: Any synthetic (TTS) narration
action: Lay a very low room-tone bed (~−45 dB) under TTS, vary the gaps between sentences inside ~300–600 ms instead of a fixed pause, and soften the top end slightly (high shelf about −2 dB).
why: Dead-silent gaps and identical pauses are a recognisable synthetic-voice signature.
evidence_note: Anti-'AI slop' checklist in cli-anything-capcut (Korean); opinion.
conflict_note: Only applies if KANG narration is TTS; recorded human narration follows R-106.

name: Dissolves are rare: keep them for time/place change
when: Choosing transitions across a video
action: Do not put a dissolve on every cut. Reserve dissolves for real time or place changes; vary cut lengths around the average shot length by roughly ±30% instead of equal lengths; plan 1–2 deliberate 2–3 s quiet/still moments per video for breath and emphasis.
why: Dissolve-on-everything, equal cut lengths and zero silence are typical auto-edit fingerprints.
evidence_note: Anti-slop checklist (cli-anything-capcut); it caps dissolves at ≤5% of transitions — opinion.
conflict_note: CONFLICT on the number: source says ≤5% dissolves; R-422 (travel/POV) allows 15–30% 'physical bridge or short dissolve'. Proposed: keep R-422's 30% ceiling for travel, adopt only the 'time/place change only' purpose test and the ±30% length variation.

name: Grade intensity caps: LUT/filter 30–50%, saturation boost ≤ +30%
when: Applying a look/filter or saturation push
action: Run creative LUTs/filters at 30–50% intensity, cap any saturation boost at about +30% (beyond that reds turn hot pink, a problem for saffron flags and temple paint), keep film grain light, and use vignettes only on dramatic scenes, not every shot.
why: Full-strength looks crush colour and are a template signature.
evidence_note: CapCut-oriented anti-slop list + mood recipes; opinion, CapCut −1..+1 scale.
conflict_note: R-266 says LUT intensity 50–70% (blend ≤55% on Rec709). Overlap is ~50%; propose 40–55% for KANG as the common band.

name: Golden-hour / warm travel look as a named starting preset
when: Sunset, ghat, beach or evening temple beats
action: Starting point (CapCut-style −1..+1 sliders, translate to FFmpeg eq/colortemperature): temperature about +0.25, highlights −0.20, shadows +0.15, contrast +0.12, saturation +0.10, brightness +0.08; optionally warm highlights / cool shadows split. A softer 'warm/café' variant: temp +0.20, contrast +0.10, sat +0.05.
why: Gives the renderer a reproducible warm look instead of ad-hoc tweaks; keeps scenes in a family.
evidence_note: Mood recipe table in cli-anything-capcut video-design.md. Slider scale is CapCut's; mapping to FFmpeg values must be calibrated on KANG test frames.
conflict_note: Subject to T-002/T-003 checks and T-023 caps.

name: Pull-out reveal may travel further than a push-in
when: Choosing Ken Burns amplitude by direction
action: Push-in on dwell/payoff stills: about 1.0→1.2 over the whole slot. Pull-out to open an act or reveal a place: start tighter (up to ~1.5) and end at 1.0 — a reveal needs more travel than an emphasis push. Let the move finish at the cut. Always within the pixel limit (G-003) and the Q-005 range.
why: A reveal reads only if enough of the frame is newly uncovered; a matching small amplitude looks like a mistake.
evidence_note: capcut-cli examples (zoom recipe) and cutcli cookbook (1.0→1.3 over 5 s). Tool recipes.
conflict_note: CONFLICT 1: amplitudes exceed G-002 (10–20%). Proposed: G-002 stays default for push-ins; allow pull-out reveals up to 1.35–1.5 only on act/chapter openers. CONFLICT 2: both sources use LINEAR interpolation (cutcli: 'linear feels most natural for Ken Burns'); G-005 says ease every move. Keep G-005 (ease) but note linear is acceptable for very slow full-slot drifts.

name: 'Unfinished pan' on the last 1–2 stills
when: Epilogue/closing stills before the end card
action: Scale the still to ~1.2 for headroom and pan horizontally about 13% of frame width, timed so the pan would finish ~1.6× the slot length — the cut arrives while the frame is still moving. Use only on the last 1–2 stills; not on hooks, not on clips under ~2 s, not on faces/action, never combined with a zoom on the same still.
why: Cutting mid-motion leaves the viewer with a 'still travelling' feeling at the end of a travel story.
evidence_note: Recipe from capcut-cli examples (keyframe-pan); craft trick, not tested.
conflict_note: Breaks G-005 'ease every move' on purpose (linear constant pan). Also check R-435 (ending: slow zoom-out + fade) — use one or the other on the last still, not both.

name: Segment entrance length by intent
when: Choosing an intro/outro animation for a still or clip
action: Fade in/out ≈ 0.5 s (default); bright flash-in ≈ 0.4 s only for reveal beats; scroll/translate-up ≈ 1.2 s for location reveals; slow zoom-out ≈ 2 s for a contextual pull-back; breathing/pulsing zoom ≈ 3 s for establishing shots; dreamy blur-out ≈ 1 s exit. Never stack two animations of the same type (two intros) on one segment, and never longer than the segment.
why: Matching animation length to purpose keeps reveals readable and avoids effect pile-ups.
evidence_note: capcut-cli animation catalogue defaults.
conflict_note: Flash-in must respect G-011 (≤3 flashes/s) and G-020 (no flash on deity frames).

name: Time-of-day labels for day-structured vlogs
when: Travel day vlog sections that follow a clock (morning darshan, noon, evening aarti)
action: Open each part of the day with a short label 'time · activity' (e.g. 'सुबह 6:00 · मंगला आरती'), give each part its own accent colour (e.g. morning yellow, noon orange, evening pink) used consistently, start the first scene with a Ken Burns so the opening is not static, and prefer wipes over dissolves between the day parts (reads like turning a page).
why: Clock labels give the viewer a timeline map for free and make day-structured travel easy to follow.
evidence_note: cutcli cookbook 'make a vlog' template; opinion.
conflict_note: Wipes are a 'motion accent' under R-422's budget; keep them to the day-part boundaries only.

name: Caption backing plate over busy footage
when: Captions or labels over busy or bright backgrounds
action: Use a semi-transparent dark rounded plate behind the text (black at ~35–55% opacity, small corner radius, ~16 px padding at 1080p) or a soft drop shadow (offset ~4–6 px, near-opaque). Choose plate for long caption lines, shadow for short pop words.
why: Plain text on variable footage fails contrast on some frames even when it passes on others.
evidence_note: Two tool recipes (cutcli knowledge-card, VectCut capcut-director).
conflict_note: G-018 contrast ratio remains the pass/fail test; the plate is the default way to meet it.

name: 9:16 type scale and line spacing
when: Text sizes for 1080×1920 reels
action: Hero/hook title ~80–135 px cap height-equivalent (pt in FFmpeg drawtext), secondary lines ~68–85, subtitles 56–64 (minimum for comfortable phone reading), micro labels 42–48 only for metadata. Multi-line text: line spacing ~0.25–0.32 em (not a tight default); separate independent text blocks by ≥115–140 px vertically.
why: Desktop-size defaults are unreadable on phones; tight leading makes Devanagari matras collide.
evidence_note: VectCutAPI capcut-director skill typography table.
conflict_note: Devanagari needs the upper end of the line-spacing band (matras/conjuncts).

name: Check text on a still at every scene boundary before delivery
when: Final QC of a render
action: Extract one frame just after every scene boundary (and mid-sentence for captions) and inspect centring, safe zone and legibility before calling the render done.
why: Text collisions and off-safe-area labels show up at boundaries where elements overlap.
evidence_note: Two tool workflows recommend it.

name: Ease the transition itself, not only the motion
when: FFmpeg xfade transitions in the KANG renderer
action: FFmpeg's xfade progresses linearly by default. Apply an easing curve to transition progress (e.g. cubic or sine in-out) — possible on stock FFmpeg through custom expressions. Avoid back/elastic easings on xfade (their overshoot is clipped or swaps the inputs).
why: Linear transitions start and stop abruptly; eased progress makes a dissolve or wipe feel smooth.
evidence_note: xfade-easing README (documented behaviour of FFmpeg xfade).
conflict_note: G-005/R-261 talk about moves and reveals; T-032 extends easing to transitions.

name: Music fade-out at the end: 0.8–1.2 s for reels, ~3 s for long-form
when: Ending of the music bed
action: Reels: smooth fade of about 0.8–1.2 s. Long-form endings: ~3 s fade with an exponential/natural curve on the final music tail.
why: An abrupt music stop sounds like a render error.
evidence_note: Two tool defaults.
